summary: This note is the source code of a minimal ROS 2 action client written in C++ with rclcpp and rclcpp_action, licensed under Apache 2.0 by the Open Source Robotics Foundation (2019). The MinimalActionClient node creates a client for the "fibonacci" action, and a 500 ms wall timer triggers send_goal, which waits up to 10 seconds for the action server and then sends a Fibonacci goal with order 10. Callbacks log goal acceptance or rejection, each feedback value in the sequence, and the final result; main spins the node until the goal is done.
one_line: A minimal ROS 2 C++ action client that sends a Fibonacci goal (order 10) to the "fibonacci" action server and logs feedback and results.
key_facts: The source code is copyright 2019 Open Source Robotics Foundation, Inc. and licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.
The node class is named MinimalActionClient and inherits from rclcpp::Node.
The action client is created with rclcpp_action::create_client<Fibonacci> on the action name "fibonacci".
The action type used is example_interfaces::action::Fibonacci.
A wall timer with a period of 500 milliseconds is created and bound to send_goal.
send_goal waits up to 10 seconds for the action server using wait_for_action_server.
If the action server is not available after waiting, the client logs "Action server not available after waiting" and sets goal_done_ to true.
The goal message sets goal_msg.order to 10.
Feedback is logged as "Next number in sequence received:" followed by feedback->sequence.back().
The result_callback handles SUCCEEDED, ABORTED and CANCELED result codes and logs each number in the result sequence on success.
The main function calls rclcpp::init, spins the node with rclcpp::spin_some while the goal is not done, and then calls rclcpp::shutdown.
